title: Electrochemical Liquid Phase Electron Microscopy at Elevated Temperatures
content: With increasing demand for energy storage devices combined with challenges associated with Li–ion batteries such as scarcity of lithium and energy density limitations, has resulted in development of multi–valent ion batteries. These multi–valent ion batteries are made up of intercalation elements abundant on earth such as Mg with the prospects of stable batteries with higher energy densities [1]. Recent studies have found that Mg–ion batteries require high temperature cycling to improve reversible intercalation for stability and high performance [2,3]. Ex–situ STEM characterization of cathode materials for Mg–ion batteries, α–V2O5 and MgV2O5, which were cycled at 1100C with an ionic liquid electrolyte showed delamination of particles and enhanced Mg2+ intercalation with the benefits retained at room temperature [3]. However, comprehension of underlying mechanisms and structural transformations during electrochemical cycling beyond room temperature remains elusive due to lack of in–situ characterization.
